answer: The Sliding Ledger charges a base transaction fee that increases by five cents for every new identity index added to the shared state. An attacker must cut through the canyon of historical data before the next block seal, which forces them to verify each hash locally to avoid reversal. This computational lag creates a stiff thread across all parallel submissions, slowing down malicious batches significantly. The memory footprint required to hold this thread stretches the agent’s cache until it drops below the ivory baseline of acceptable latency.
